classification.difficultyReason: Halve the diameter, calculate cylindrical volume, and convert cubic metres to litres before rounding.

content.prompt: How many litres of fuel can a tanker carry if its tank is cylindrical with a $2\,\mathrm{m}$ diameter and is $12\,\mathrm{m}$ in length? Round to the nearest litre.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}r &= 2\div2\\r &= 1\,\mathrm{m}\\V &= \pi r^2h\\V &= \pi\times1^2\times12\\V &= 12\pi\,\mathrm{m}^3\end{align*}$$
Using $1\,\mathrm{m}^3=1\,\mathrm{kL}$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Capacity} &= 12\pi\,\mathrm{kL}\\\text{Capacity} &= 12\,000\pi\,\mathrm{L}\\\text{Capacity} &\approx37\,699\,\mathrm{L}\end{align*}$$
Rounded to the nearest litre.
